title: He Is Thirty-Nine. On Saturday, He Will Become the Oldest Indian to Play an ODI.
excerpt: Rohit Sharma will surpass Mohinder Amarnath's 37-year-old record when he takes the field in Dharamsala for the first ODI against Afghanistan.
body:
When Rohit Sharma walks out to bat in Dharamsala on Saturday for the first ODI against Afghanistan, he will make a piece of history before he even faces a delivery. At 39 years and 44 days, the Hitman will become the oldest Indian cricketer to play a One-Day International, breaking a record that has stood untouched since 1989.

The man he overtakes is Mohinder Amarnath, the gritty all-rounder who played his last ODI for India at 39 years and 36 days. Amarnath's record has survived the careers of Tendulkar, Dravid, Ganguly, Dhoni, and every other Indian great who came after him. Until now.

## A Record That Outlived Generations

The longevity of Amarnath's mark tells its own story. Indian cricket has cycled through six coaches, three World Cup campaigns, and the entire IPL era since the record was set. That it took nearly four decades for someone to surpass it speaks to how unusual it is for an Indian batter to remain at the top of the ODI game this deep into his thirties.

Rohit's continued selection is not a sentimental gesture. He was cleared by the BCCI's Centre of Excellence and has been sweating it out in the nets at Mohali alongside captain Shubman Gill and the rest of the squad. The Indian team departed for Dharamsala on Thursday, and the mood in the camp is buoyant after their innings-and-300-run demolition of Afghanistan in the one-off Test at New Chandigarh.

## The IPL Was Unkind. This Series Is Redemption.

Rohit's IPL 2026 campaign was one to forget — 283 runs in nine matches with a highest score of just 26, compounded by a hamstring injury that forced him to miss games. For any other 39-year-old, those numbers would have been a quiet career coda. But the selectors, and head coach Gautam Gambhir, clearly see something different in the ODI format.

In ODIs, Rohit's record against Afghanistan is immaculate. He is India's leading run-scorer against them in the format, with 150 runs across their limited head-to-head encounters. The three-match series — Dharamsala on June 13, Lucknow on June 17, Chennai on June 20 — is India's first bilateral ODI series against Afghanistan, and it doubles as the start of a 20-ODI runway to the 2027 World Cup.

## A Squad Built for the Future, Led by the Past

The squad Rohit walks into is unmistakably transitional. Virat Kohli is out with a hamstring injury. Hardik Pandya has been ruled out with a quadriceps strain. Shubman Gill captains the side for the first time in a bilateral ODI series, with three uncapped players — Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, and Harsh Dubey — all in the mix for debuts.

In that context, Rohit's presence is not just a statistical footnote. He is the bridge between what Indian cricket was and what it is becoming. The young players in the dressing room — many of whom grew up idolising him — will have the Hitman at the other end of the pitch when they walk out for their first international innings.

For NRI fans scattered across North America, the UK, and the Gulf, Saturday's match starts at a civilised hour — 1:30 PM IST, or roughly 4 AM Eastern. Set the alarm. You may not get many more chances to watch Rohit Sharma in India colours.

## What Comes Next

The overall record for the oldest Indian international cricketer belongs to Vinoo Mankad, who played at 41 years and 300 days. Rohit is still two years and change from that. Nobody is saying he will get there. But nobody expected him to get here, either.

The three ODIs against Afghanistan will answer several questions about India's 2027 World Cup squad. The first question, though, is simpler: can a 39-year-old Rohit Sharma, eight months removed from a poor IPL, still summon the timing and the hunger that made him the most destructive opener in ODI history?

Dharamsala will tell.
